title: Outcome Goals Are Overrated
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article distinguishes two goal types leaders often conflate: Outcome goals, which depend on external factors and other people's performance, and Performance goals, which are fully within an individual's control and measure progress against a baseline. The author argues that leaders over-rely on Outcome goals, which turns effort into a pass/fail proposition and demoralizes people when external circumstances derail an otherwise strong performance. Performance goals, by contrast, sustain motivation because progress is visible and attributable to effort. The piece closes by urging leaders to audit their own goal-setting habits and rebalance toward performance-based targets.
points: Outcome goals (winning, promotion, market share) depend heavily on external factors and other people's performance, making them poor drivers of sustained motivation.
Performance goals are fully within an individual's control and measure progress against a baseline, which is what makes them more motivating day to day.
Leaders who set only outcome goals turn every effort into a binary pass/fail, which demoralizes teams when external factors sink a good performance.
The best leaders pair both goal types: outcome goals set direction and stakes, while performance goals keep people grounded in immediate, controllable action.
quotes: These goals focus on the end result of a competition, event, or initiative. As such, they are highly dependent on external factors and the performance of others.
Performance goals are completely within the control of those who pursue them and typically reflect progress or improvement against a baseline, target, or record.
Because people control how they perform, the goals they set regarding their performance provide a roadmap of progress.
Leaders who only set Outcome goals pressurize performance. Because everything becomes judged against the attainment of the outcome, the stakes are extremely high and represent a Pass/Fail.
While Outcome goals are important for setting direction and highlighting the ultimate prize worth struggling for, Performance goals keep people grounded in what they need to do now to succeed.
